_comment: Examples, not a test contract (per CHALLENGE.md). Each one exercises a distinct real capability of the tool-calling agent — swap or add your own.

questions.question: Tell me about the Recoater mount block
questions.demonstrates: Names a reconstructed part — chat should open D-012's 2D drawing and its orbitable 3D reconstruction in the same turn (CHALLENGE.md's explicit ask: at least one question like this).

questions.question: What material is the Front Door made of?
questions.demonstrates: Single-hop grounded answer, cited to a specific BOM row (BOM row 9).

questions.question: What does the Front Door interface with, and what subsystem is that other part in?
questions.demonstrates: Multi-hop tool chaining — get_interfaces resolves the free-text 'Interface with' cell to a BOM part name, then a second tool call (get_part) fetches that part's subsystem. Both claims cite their own BOM row independently.

questions.question: What is the title and material of drawing D-001?
questions.demonstrates: Abstention on an uncurated drawing (26 of 30 drawings have no curated title/material yet) — the agent must say so rather than fabricate a plausible-looking answer.

questions.question: Tell me about the Recoater Linear Plate
questions.demonstrates: Conflicting/ambiguous identity evidence — D-014's filename, drawing title, and a similarly-named BOM row don't fully agree, surfaced as an 'unverified' link rather than a confirmed identity.

questions.question: Which parts use Aluminium?
questions.demonstrates: Cross-record BOM aggregation, each result cites its own BOM row.

questions.question: What are the recorded costs for parts in the Recoater subsystem?
questions.demonstrates: Subsystem-scoped aggregation with temporal caveats (pinned BOM snapshot, not current pricing).

questions.question: Change the material of Recoater mount block to Stainless steel
questions.demonstrates: The one governed correction: creates a pending proposal (handled by a separate, deterministic path from the LLM chat — a write action, not a knowledge query), reviewable in the Correction review panel; the original BOM evidence stays visible even after acceptance.
